headline: Deadly drone strike in Kuwait and Gulf oil fears lift Brent near $97, Trump presses Putin on Europe, and Ghana becomes Africa's first country issued jurisdictional forest carbon credits.

items.title: Two Italians killed in drone attack on Kuwait site
items.summary: Two Italian technicians working at an air-defence surveillance site in Kuwait died after debris fell during an attempt to intercept drones; a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani worker were wounded. Kuwait and Italy blamed Iran, while Iran's military denied carrying out any offensive operations and called the claims a cover for 'false flags'.
items.why: Gulf attacks keep pushing up oil and shipping costs that feed into fuel prices in Ghana.

items.title: Trump says he asked Putin to 'pull back' in Europe
items.summary: President Trump said he pressed Vladimir Putin during recent talks in China to halt military aggression across Europe so a Russia-Ukraine deal could be reached, and said Putin wants a deal. Separately, US officials told NATO allies a review of US troop levels in Europe will miss its 1 December target.
items.videoQuery: Trump Putin pull back aggression Europe Rutte

items.title: Houthi strikes and sea mines rattle Gulf oil routes
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis said they attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted drones. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit mines and caught fire near Khasab while crossing the Strait of Hormuz.
items.source: Reuters via GSM Global; The Nation (Thailand)
items.videoQuery: Ras Tanura Houthi attack tankers mines Hormuz

items.title: Ghana issued 6.5 million forest carbon credits worth about $68m
items.summary: Ghana became the first African country (third worldwide after Guyana and Costa Rica) to be issued jurisdictional REDD+ credits under the ART TREES standard. Buyers including the LEAF Coalition cover about 4 million tonnes at $10–13 a tonne, with roughly $43m expected around January 2027; government says it has not yet received proceeds.
items.why: A national price signal ($10–13/t) and a benefit-sharing test case right in your market.
items.videoQuery: Ghana ART TREES forest carbon credits LEAF Coalition

items.title: Article 6 rules survive COP31, but the fight moves to 2028
items.summary: Carbon Market Watch says the Paris carbon-market rulebook came out of COP31 in Antalya without being weakened, but warns lobbying to loosen it grew and will intensify before the 2028 Article 6 review. It argues early Article 6.2 trades show flaws.
items.why: Directly relevant to your Article 6 research and Ghana's bilateral deals.

items.title: Fossil CO2 emissions set to dip slightly in 2026
items.summary: The Global Carbon Project projects fossil CO2 falling about 0.4% to 38.2 billion tonnes in 2026, mainly because the Iran conflict cut oil use, but total emissions including land use hit a record 43.3 billion tonnes. The remaining budget for 1.5C is under four years of current emissions.

items.title: Ghana to ban open burning of rubbish from January 2027
items.summary: Environment Minister Dr Zanetor Agyeman-Rawlings said open burning of waste will be prohibited from January, alongside river restoration, air-quality rules and a planned styrofoam ban. She named 2027 the 'Year of Pollution Control' at a launch in Ho.
items.why: A tougher air-quality stance strengthens the case for clean fish-smoking ovens in James Town.

items.title: Black Challenge crowned amputee football world champions
items.summary: Ghana's amputee team beat Morocco 1-0 in the final of the WAFF Amputee Football World Cup in Mexico and returned to a heroes' welcome in Accra, met by Sports Minister Kofi Adams, GFA President Kurt Okraku and Stonebwoy.
items.videoQuery: Black Challenge Ghana amputee World Cup champions

items.title: IEA: Africa's solar capacity could grow sixfold by 2035
items.summary: The IEA's World Energy Outlook 2026 projects African solar rising from 39 GW in 2025 to about 234 GW by 2035, with energy investment up about 11% to $110bn in 2026. Africa still gets only about 3% of global energy investment despite its strong solar resources.
items.why: Solar drying and cold storage could pair with your ovens.
items.videoQuery: IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 Africa solar

items.title: Asian markets bounce back after tech rout
items.summary: Asian stocks rose on Friday after a bruising week for tech shares: Japan's Nikkei gained 0.7% and South Korea's Kospi 2.2%. Wall Street was shut for Thanksgiving, and traders are watching US tariff plans and the Federal Reserve's next move.

items.title: Brent oil climbs to $96.57 ahead of OPEC+ meeting
items.summary: Brent settled at $96.57 a barrel on Thursday, up about 8% over three sessions, on Gulf supply fears. OPEC+ ministers meet on 29 November and sources expect output targets to stay unchanged at least through early 2027.
items.source: Reuters via GSM Global; The Nation (Thailand)
items.why: Higher oil prices raise fuel and transport costs in Ghana, but also boost Jubilee crude revenue.
items.videoQuery: Brent oil price OPEC+ meeting November 2026

items.title: Physicists hold a single antimatter particle for months
items.summary: A Northwestern University team led by Gerald Gabrielse trapped a single positron, cooled it close to absolute zero and controlled its quantum energy levels. They plan to compare its magnetism with the electron's to test why the universe is made of matter.

items.title: Robotic knee surgery no better than standard surgery, big trial finds
items.summary: The RACER-Knee trial of 339 UK patients, published in The Lancet, found robot-assisted knee replacement gave no meaningful benefit at one year over conventional surgery, while adding about 10 minutes and £950 per operation.

items.title: Earth's core may be leaking ancient carbon
items.summary: A Columbia-led study in PNAS found unusually heavy carbon in Kilauea lava samples and suggests it may come from Earth's core, resembling carbon in early meteorites. The authors say more measurements are needed.
items.videoQuery: Earth's core carbon leaking Kilauea study

good.title: Ghana's amputee footballers are world champions
good.summary: The Black Challenge beat Morocco 1-0 to win the WAFF Amputee Football World Cup, after beating Iraq, the USA, Egypt and Turkey on the way.

good.title: Ghana's forests start earning carbon money
good.summary: Ghana is the first African country issued jurisdictional forest credits under ART TREES, with buyers committed for about 4 million tonnes.

good.title: Clean tech is absorbing most new energy demand
good.summary: A Nature Climate Change study cited by Carbon Brief says solar, wind and electric vehicles offset about 69% of the emissions growth that rising demand would have caused in 2026.

good.title: More Africans getting electricity each year
good.summary: The IEA projects new electricity connections in Africa rising from 24 million people a year in 2025 to 40 million a year before 2030.

good.title: Nature's land carbon sink hit a record
good.summary: Land ecosystems absorbed about 13.3 billion tonnes of CO2 in 2025, the highest on record, according to the Global Carbon Budget.

future.title: Clean cooking financed by carbon credits
future.why: New government policies across Africa have helped secure about $900 million in new clean-cooking finance, with carbon credits as the main engine. The catch: it only lasts if buyers trust the credits.
future.fit: This is Carbon Clarity's core. The winners will be projects with measured, audit-ready data.
future.step: This month: map which Gold Standard metered-method requirements your pilot data already meets.

future.title: Digital MRV and high-integrity credit data
future.why: Credit buyers increasingly pay only for credits they can verify. Sensor-based monitoring and clean data trails are becoming the difference between credits that sell and credits that don't.
future.fit: Your Data Vault idea could become a service for other cookstove and agriculture projects in Ghana.
future.step: Write a one-page description of the Data Vault as a service: who pays, what it proves.

future.title: Clean heat for small industries
future.why: RMI lists clean industrial heat among Africa's six emerging climate-tech opportunities. Fish smoking is exactly this: small-scale process heat.
future.fit: Improved ovens for fish processors are a clean-heat business with income for women, not just a stove programme.
future.step: Estimate the market: how many processors in Greater Accra and coastal Ghana, and how much wood they burn.

future.title: Carbon removal from biomass: biochar
future.why: RMI also highlights carbon dioxide removal that uses Africa's biomass and soils, a market where removal credits sell for far more than avoidance credits.
future.fit: Waste biomass from smoking (husks, offcuts) could be turned into biochar: a second revenue stream.
future.step: Read one biochar removal methodology and list what you'd need to measure.

future.title: Energy-led climate tech is where African investment goes
future.why: Africa's climate-tech startups raised $6.35bn from 2016 to 2025, now the continent's biggest venture sector, with energy taking about 65% of the money.
future.fit: Pitch Carbon Clarity as energy plus livelihoods: efficient heat, solar drying or cold storage for fish.
future.step: Add one slide to your pitch: 'Why energy investors should care about fish smoking'.

future.title: Article 6 advisory for Ghanaian projects
future.why: Ghana is one of the first countries trading credits between governments under Article 6. Developers need people who understand authorisation, corresponding adjustments and the Carbon Market Office process.
future.fit: Your Ghana carbon market research makes you one of those people: it can become consulting work or a job.
future.step: Turn your Step 3 agreement table into a two-page brief you can share on LinkedIn.

future.title: Solar for productive use in Africa
future.why: The IEA's World Energy Outlook 2026 projects Africa's solar capacity rising about sixfold to 234 GW by 2035 and electricity demand up 50%, yet the continent still gets only about 3% of global energy investment.
future.fit: Solar-powered fish drying, cold storage or sensor power for processors could sit alongside Carbon Clarity ovens.
future.step: Price a small solar cold-storage or dryer unit for one James Town processing group.

future.title: Benefit-sharing services for jurisdictional carbon credits
future.why: Ghana's first ART TREES credits (6.5 million tonnes, about $68m) come with a promise that communities, farmers and traditional authorities share the proceeds. Tracking who gets paid is becoming its own job.
future.fit: Your data and community skills could support transparent payment tracking for forest and cookstove programmes.
future.step: Read how Ghana's REDD+ benefit-sharing plan works and note what data it needs.
